facts.text: The workspace groups the full LeRobot humanoid project from design to deployment, including mechanical/control co-design, hardware build assets, robot model assets, the runtime and deployment stack, and simulation-based identification
Each folder of the workspace is an independent Git repository with its own history and remotes
The project aims to build an open and practical low-cost humanoid robot that people can reproduce
The hardware cost target is less than USD 5,000, depending on sourcing, shipping and taxes
The design prioritizes 3D-printed custom mechanical parts that are printable and documented
The lerobot-humanoid-model repository provides versioned MJCF/URDF robot model assets and Python helpers (lerobot_humanoid_models) that the runtime and identification repositories consume
The lerobot-humanoid-runtime repository makes the robot move in simulation and on real hardware, with controllers, calibration, policy execution and deployment
The lerobot-humanoid-identification repository replays real logs and tunes simulator parameters with batched replay and CMA-ES identification
The workspace was initially developed by Virgile Batto during his time at Hugging Face LeRobot

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it reads the scene for the actuator control ranges and the qpos/qvel dimensions but integrates a placeholder velocity proportional to each control value, so trajectories, contacts, friction and actuator dynamics are not MuJoCo's
the scene includes robot.xml and the model's meshes, materials and collision shapes are not loaded by the stand-in; no contact, equality, tendon or actuator constraint of the model is resolved
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine
only the first card model, the bipedal_plateform scene, is served; the no-arms and lerobot_humanoide variants and the identification copies are other devices and are not part of this driver
the upstream runtime, identification and hardware stacks are not part of this driver; it exposes only the MuJoCo ctrl vector and integration state, with no viewer or rendering
no physical robot is modelled and nothing was validated against the LeRobot humanoid hardware

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
